evidence: Verg. G. 1.338: annua magnae sacra refer Cererī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Both senses of English annual: what comes round every year (annua sacra, the yearly rites) and what lasts a year (an office held for a year, Caes. BG 1.16.5). As a noun, annua (n. pl.) is a yearly allowance, a pension (see pension). Every year, as an adverb, is quotannīs (see every year).

evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4, of rites and of feast days (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of what recurs at the same time each year: rites, feast days, the turn of the seasons. English anniversary comes from it; a birthday is diēs nātālis (see birthday).

phrases.latin: tū cursū, dea, mēnstruō mētiēns iter annuum
phrases.english: you, goddess, measuring out the year’s journey by your monthly course

phrases.latin: quī summō magistrātuī praeerat, quem vergobretum appellant Haeduī, quī creātur annuus et vītae necisque in suōs habet potestātem
phrases.english: who held the highest office, which the Haedui call the vergobret: he is elected for a year and has the power of life and death over his people
